newsitem.title: USA: PSE&G offers new gas rates to NJ customers.
newsitem.headline: PSE&G offers new gas rates to NJ customers.

text.p: Beginning April 1, residential natural gas customers in New Jersey will be able to choose a supplier other than New Jersey Natural Gas Co (NJNG), Public Service Electric and Gas Co said Monday.

PSE&G, as part of NJNG's "Natural Choice" gas pilot program aimed at opening the utility market to more competition, will be vying for residential customers next month in Monmouth, Ocean, Morris and Middlesex Counties.
The utility said it will offer gas at a rate of 35 cents per therm, which PSE&G estimated will result in a 13 percent drop from their current rates.
The initial enrollment period for the program will be limited to the first 5,000 customers.
NJNG will continue to deliver the gas until this September when the newly chosen provider will assume responsibility.
An additional 5,000 customers will be allowed to choose an alternate energy provider during a second enrollment period in November.
Though this is the first gas choice program offered to New Jersey's residential customers, a large group of commercial and industrial customers have already joined the program.
Under the state's restructuring plan, the residential electricity market is slated to be open to competition from October 1998.
